item.title: AI Agents, From Chatbot to Production
item.author: 15989119660@163.com (Xiangtao XIAO)
item.description:
AI Agents, From Chatbot to Production

An AI agent is the LLM application taken further — something that can plan on its own, carry out tasks, and interact with its environment.

Foundational papers:

item.title: Prompt Engineering
item.author: 15989119660@163.com (Xiangtao XIAO)
item.description:
Prompt Engineering

https://www.coursera.org/learn/chatgpt-prompt-engineering-for-developers-project/home/welcome

Prompt engineering is the practice of designing and refining the input you give a large language model so it produces the output you actually want. It took off after GPT-3 came out, and it’s basically the bridge between what a user wants and what the model can do.

Key papers:

  • Brown, T. B., et al. (2020). “Language Models are Few-Shot Learners.” NeurIPS. [link] — the GPT-3 paper, the first to really demonstrate the potential of prompt engineering
  • Wei, J., et al. (2022). “Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models.” NeurIPS. [link]

1. Prompting Principles

Principle 1: Write clear and specific instructions

Clarity and specificity are the two things that matter most when writing a prompt. Vague instructions tend to produce unpredictable outputs, while specific ones noticeably improve output quality.

item.title: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
item.author: 15989119660@163.com (Xiangtao XIAO)
item.description:
RAG

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) combines information retrieval with text generation — it pulls in an external knowledge base to make an LLM’s answers better.

Foundational papers:

  • Lewis, P., et al. (2020). “Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks.” NeurIPS. [paper] — the paper that started RAG
  • Guu, K., et al. (2020). “REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training.” ICML. [paper]
  • Izacard, G., & Grave, É. (2021). “Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering.” EACL. [paper] — a different take on RAG

1. Context Window

What it is

The context window is the maximum amount of text an LLM can read and reason over in a single pass.

item.title: A Tour of Payment Methods on Chinese E-Commerce Platforms
item.author: 15989119660@163.com (Xiangtao XIAO)
item.description:
1. Comparing the mainstream payment methods

1. Business-to-business cash transfer

How it works: an initiated transfer from a bank counter or corporate online banking, or a payment through a bank’s fund-splitting system with a receipt.

Limits: large transfers are possible. Anything above RMB 50,000 goes through the PBOC’s large-value payment system, which doesn’t run on weekends and holidays, and can be affected accordingly (on weekdays it runs from 20:30 the previous evening through 17:15 the same day).

item.title: A First Look at Cross-Border Payments
item.author: 15989119660@163.com (Xiangtao XIAO)
item.description:
Notes from working through Cross-Border E-Commerce Payment and Settlement, my starting point for getting into cross-border payments.

A few basic concepts

Foreign exchange (FX)

Foreign exchange is a claim held by a country’s monetary authorities — the central bank, currency management bodies, exchange stabilization funds, and the treasury — in the form of bank deposits, treasury bills, and short- and long-term government securities, that can be drawn on to cover a balance-of-payments deficit. It covers foreign currency itself, foreign-currency deposits, foreign-currency securities (government bonds, treasury bills, corporate bonds, stocks), and foreign-currency payment instruments such as drafts, bank certificates of deposit, and postal savings certificates.

item.title: What I'd Tell a New Product Manager on Day One

Wrapping up what to prepare for when you’re new to a job, and the mistakes I made so I don’t forget them.

1. Get your tools set up

Find out what software the company runs on day to day. If IT already has it installed for you, great. If it’s something you’ve never used, learn the basics when you have a spare moment, or just ask a colleague.

2. Learn how the place actually works

item.title: Notes on Requirement Analysis and Management
item.author: 15989119660@163.com (Xiangtao XIAO)
item.description: When you’re digging into what users actually need, it’s rarely something concrete and explicit. There’s the old Ford line — “if I’d asked people what they wanted, they’d have said a faster horse” — but once you get to actually building the product, you still have to land on something concrete: specific features that satisfy the underlying need. So what I mean by “requirement analysis and management” here is the whole chain: start from a surface-level ask, dig into the real need underneath it, evaluate it, land on a specific solution, and hand that off to engineers and designers to turn into an actual product. B2B and B2C products differ quite a bit in how this plays out.

item.title: Notes on Doing Competitive Analysis
item.author: 15989119660@163.com (Xiangtao XIAO)
item.description:
1 Why Bother with Competitive Analysis

1. Better decisions. Understanding competitors’ products helps you position your own — and steer clear of the strongest players so you don’t wander into a red ocean. It lowers the risk of getting your bets wrong.

2. Learning from others. Studying what makes a competitor’s product strong lets you build more deliberately: take what works, absorb their strengths, and use it to sharpen your own edge.
